lessons.title: Linked List Basics
lessons.concept: A linked list is nodes linked via pointers, allowing dynamic memory use. Singly linked: each node points to next. Access is O(n); insert/delete at known position O(1).
lessons.formula: Access: O(n); Insert/Delete at known node: O(1)
lessons.worked_example: Reverse singly linked list: use three pointers (prev, curr, next); reverse links iteratively.
mistakes: Forgetting to save next before reversing

lessons.title: Linked List vs Array
lessons.concept: Array: O(1) access, O(n) insert/delete (shift). Linked list: O(n) access, O(1) insert/delete at known node, no random access.
lessons.formula: Array access O(1); LL access O(n)
lessons.worked_example: Frequent insertions/deletions → linked list better. Frequent random access → array better.
mistakes: Choosing array for frequent middle insertions

practice.question: Better for frequent insertions and deletions?
practice.explanation: Linked lists support O(1) insertion/deletion at known positions; arrays require shifting O(n).

questions.question: Data structure for to-do list where tasks added at end and processed in order added?
questions.explanation: Processed in order added → First-In-First-Out → Queue.

questions.question: Structure for managing function calls and local variables?
questions.explanation: Function call stack uses LIFO → stack.

questions.question: Structure for BFS in graph traversal?
questions.explanation: BFS uses a queue (FIFO) to explore level by level.

questions.question: Time to insert at end of singly linked list with tail pointer?
questions.explanation: With tail pointer, append directly → O(1).
